title: NIST SSDF 1.1: Component Governance and Release Provenance

summary: NIST's SSDF 1.1 describes how to select, maintain and assess software components throughout their use. Practices PW.4.1 and PW.4.4 cover organizational requirements, component integrity, vulnerabilities and maintenance status. PS.3.2 links release records to evidence of where components came from.
defensive_use: Give each dependency an owner, acceptance requirements, provenance records, and a plan for maintenance or replacement. Revisit these decisions throughout the component’s lifetime. Make the boundary between external supplier evidence and the organization’s own release decision explicit.
prerequisites: Software development lifecycle and release familiarity

caveats: This is a risk-based high-level framework, not a product certification or an exhaustive technical recipe.
At review, NIST lists SSDF 1.1 as Final and SSDF 1.2 as an Initial Public Draft dated 2025-12-17. The draft’s status and dates must not be merged into this edition’s record.
